thresholds.label: `RER` per dataset (Trinity A.6 eq. 14)
thresholds.note: The paper's own pool-selection criterion. E(D, M) is accuracy on a whole dataset, so this is much smaller than the per-question number and must be judged on its own scale.

thresholds.label: `RER` per question (vs Per-Question-Best, Fig. 3)
thresholds.note: Headroom against the per-question oracle. Reported because it is what a per-question router could theoretically capture; never quote it as the A.6 number.

thresholds.label: Datasets in the reward matrix
thresholds.note: `RER` per dataset is meaningless with one dataset: Z and S* collapse to the same value.

thresholds.label: Tasks where all agents score equal
thresholds.note: Fugu-Lite V1 scored 0.753 here and its router learned 'always pick Gemini'.

thresholds.label: Tasks with a unique best agent
Weakest agent's uniquely-best share, x pool size
thresholds.note: 1.0 means the weakest agent is uniquely best exactly as often as a uniform draw predicts. Scaled by pool size so one threshold holds for 4 or 7 agents. Below 0.1 that agent is dead weight in the action space.

thresholds.label: Worst agent's empty-response rate
thresholds.note: 88 of Fugu-Lite's 900 DeepSeek calls were HTTP 200 with empty content.

thresholds.label: Worst agent's call-error rate
thresholds.note: Errors score as wrong answers and silently depress that agent's reward.
